basic_identification.full_title: Classification and Acceptance Tests for Bare Solid Wire Electrodes and Wire Flux Combination for Submerged Arc Welding of Structural Steel — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering / Welding General (approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Welding General Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements for the classification and acceptance testing of bare solid wire electrodes and wire-flux combinations used in submerged arc welding (SAW) of structural steels. It applies specifically to carbon steel and medium tensile steel weldments with tensile strength up to 700 N/mm² and sulfur/phosphorus content limited to a maximum of 0.06 percent each.

revision_history.edition: First Edition (officially formulated to merge and supersede the legacy specifications of IS 7280 : 1974 and IS 3613 : 1974)

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Unlike structural steel sections or builders hardware which are subject to mandatory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), welding electrodes and wire-flux combinations under IS 15977 are certified on a voluntary basis. Manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on wire drums, spools, and flux bags. However, compliance with this standard is universally mandated inside public, railway, and defense structural fabrication tenders.

requirements.detail: Every commercial tag, coil label, or bag of flux conforming to this standard may be marked with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).
Filler wires must be classified on the basis of their chemical composition. In the standard designation (e.g. S-X), the prefix 'S' represents a solid wire electrode.
Specifies standard wire diameters: 1.6, 2.0, 2.4, 3.2, 4.0, 5.0, 6.3, and 8.0 mm. The diameter tolerance is strictly capped at ±0.05 mm.

To establish dimensional uniformity, wire diameter must be calculated as the average of six readings: two measurements taken at 90 degrees to each other at one location, repeated at three distinct locations spaced 300 mm apart.

Submerged arc welding fluxes are granular and classified by their chemical constituents (e.g. Symbol 'MS' denotes Manganese-Silicate flux containing MnO + SiO2 >= 50% minimum and CaO <= 15% maximum; 'CS' denotes Calcium-Silicate).

requirements.requirement_type: Four-Part Performance Code and Impact Symbols (Table 5)
requirements.detail: Establishes a standardized symbol coding system defining mechanical properties. The fourth part indicates the Charpy V-notch impact testing temperature: Symbol 1 (Room temperature, approx 20°C), Symbol 2 (0 ± 1°C), Symbol 3 (-20 ± 1°C), and Symbol 4 (-40 ± 1°C).

Deposited weld metal must undergo radiographic inspection to verify soundness prior to mechanical testing. The weld must show zero cracks, zero incomplete fusion, zero incomplete penetration, and restrict slag inclusions (no slag line longer than 8 mm or groups totaling more than 25 mm in a 300 mm length).
Test weld assemblies must be welded in the downhand position using a multi-run technique without post-weld heat treatment. Wire-flux combinations suitable for both AC and DC must be tested on AC.

Four transverse bend specimens (face and root bends) must be tested. The weldment satisfies the code if bent 120° over a former having a diameter equal to 3 times the specimen thickness, with zero cracks/defects exceeding 3 mm across or 1.5 mm along length.

Weldments must meet specified minimum impact energy values (e.g. 47 J for T31–T34). If the average of three specimens falls slightly below the threshold (between 34 J and 40 J), three additional specimens must be tested and added to the average. If the six-specimen average meets the limit, the combination complies.
Specified acceptance tests must be repeated at intervals not exceeding 12 months to verify continuous quality and product homogeneity.
The date of manufacture and production control test results of any supplied wire-flux combination must be completely traceable through its unique batch or lot number.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15977 : 2013 is the national Indian Standard specification governing the classification and acceptance testing of bare solid wire electrodes and wire-flux combinations used in submerged arc welding (SAW) of structural steels. Certified on a voluntary basis under the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) scheme, this code regulates standard wire dimensions (1.6 to 8.0 mm), wire chemistry, and flux composition categories (such as manganese-silicate or calcium-silicate). To ensure structural safety in heavy infrastructure (such as bridges, boilers, and high-tensile structures), the standard enforces rigorous mechanical and non-destructive quality boundaries—including multi-pass downhand test plate welding (without post-weld heat treatment), radiographic checks for micro-cracks and slag inclusions, and transverse butt-weld bend tests up to 120° alongside low-temperature Charpy V-notch impact toughness evaluations.
